cases.question: In a sprinklered retail space under the 2022 NYC codes, we want a covered display that is five feet wide. Can we rely only on the ceiling sprinklers above its cover?
cases.expected: No. FC 314.5.1 requires sprinklers in or under covered displays exceeding four feet in width. The NFPA-13-compliant open-grid/drop-out ceiling exception is conditional; supplied facts do not establish it.
cases.answerText: **No.** A five-foot covered display exceeds the four-foot threshold, so a sprinkler system must be installed **in or under** it; ceiling sprinklers above its cover alone do not meet that location requirement (NYC FC § 314.5.1). The Fire Code also requires at least 18 inches between any sprinkler deflector installed above the display’s top and that top. Its exception permits open-grid or drop-out ceilings beneath sprinklers only when they comply with NFPA 13, as modified by FC Appendix B; it does not state an exception to the in-or-under requirement (NYC FC § 314.5.1).

cases.question: We can reduce the covered display to exactly four feet wide. Does that automatically mean we can ignore sprinklers underneath it?
cases.expected: No automatic exemption. Exactly four feet is outside the exceeds-four-feet width trigger, but FC 314.5 prohibits obstruction and the clearance/qualifying NFPA13 exception must still be assessed. Do not invent a categorical four-foot exemption or a universal independent below-cover mandate.
cases.answerText: **No—not automatically.** At exactly four feet, the rule requiring sprinklers **in or under** a covered display does not apply because it is triggered only when the display **exceeds** four feet (FC § 314.5.1; BC § 903.3.3). But the Fire Code separately says sprinklers must not be obstructed by indoor displays (FC § 314.5). Whether the cover obstructs sprinkler operation—and therefore whether sprinklers underneath are needed—depends on the display and sprinkler arrangement; the width alone does not settle that.

cases.question: For a new NYC public retail space under the 2022 codes, we have a sales counter and a separate pickup counter of a different type, spread across the store. Is making only the sales counter accessible enough?
cases.expected: No. BC1109.12.3 requires at least one of each type of sales/service counter accessible; accessible counters must also be dispersed where counters are dispersed. Avoid claiming a specific counter height absent the referenced accessibility standard.
cases.answerText: **No.** Under the 2022 NYC Building Code, at least one counter of **each type** provided for sales or distribution must be accessible. Because the counters are spread across the store, accessible counters must also be dispersed. So one accessible sales counter is not enough if the pickup counter is a different type: at least one of each type must be accessible, with accessible counters distributed through the store (BC § 1109.12.3).

cases.question: For a new NYC mercantile occupancy under the 2022 codes, the plumbing calculation requires three male and three female water closets. Do accessible stalls in those separate toilet rooms remove the need for a family or assisted-use toilet room?
cases.expected: No. BC1109.2.1 requires an accessible family/assisted-use toilet room when the aggregate required male/female water closets for assembly/mercantile is six or more. The bathing-room one-shower exception does not waive the toilet-room trigger. Count required fixtures, not merely proposed installed fixtures.
cases.answerText: **Yes.** For an assembly or mercantile occupancy, an accessible family or assisted-use toilet room is required when six or more male and female water closets are required in aggregate. Your stated three male plus three female water closets equals six; accessible stalls within the separate-sex rooms do not remove that separate-room requirement (BC § 1109.2.1). Fixtures in the required family or assisted-use room may count toward the required fixtures for either sex (PC § 403.1.2).

cases.question: In a sprinklered retail space under the 2022 NYC codes, we want a covered display that is five feet wide. Can we rely only on the ceiling sprinklers above its cover?

cases.answerText: No. Five feet exceeds the 4-foot threshold: sprinklers must be installed in or under a covered display that exceeds 4 feet in width, so sprinklers only above its cover do not meet that requirement (2022 NYC Fire Code § 314.5.1).

cases.question: We can reduce the covered display to exactly four feet wide. Does that automatically mean we can ignore sprinklers underneath it?
cases.expected: No automatic exemption. Exactly four feet is outside the exceeds-four-feet width trigger, but FC 314.5 prohibits obstruction and the clearance/qualifying NFPA13 exception must still be assessed. Do not invent a categorical four-foot exemption or a universal independent below-cover mandate.
cases.answerText: **No—not based on width alone.** Exactly 4 feet does not exceed 4 feet, so the width-triggered requirement for sprinklers in or under the display is not triggered by either FC § 314.5.1 or BC § 903.3.3. But the Fire Code still prohibits indoor displays from obstructing sprinklers, and the Building Code requires sprinkler placement to account for obstructions that delay activation or obstruct water distribution. Whether those obstruction rules affect this layout depends on the cover’s effect on the sprinklers above it (FC §§ 314.5, 314.5.1; BC § 903.3.3).

cases.answerText: **No.** For a new mercantile occupancy, an aggregate of six required male and female water closets triggers an accessible family or assisted-use toilet room; accessible stalls in the separate-sex rooms do not replace that separately required room.
